episode_title: From Family Pest Control to $52M: Chase Hazelwood on Growth, Acquisitions, and AI-Driven Service

real_qa.q: How did Chase Hazelwood grow Go Forth Pest Control from $2.5 million to $52 million in revenue?
real_qa.r: Hazelwood transitioned from working in the business to working on it by implementing modern technology, automation, and online systems in 2018. He created checklists and processes for every customer interaction, implemented a 24-hour service guarantee, and developed a mobile device management system allowing technicians to operate remotely. He also adopted a sales philosophy where service is sales and trained all employees in consultative customer interaction, rather than recruiting dedicated salespeople.
real_qa.requete: How did Chase Hazelwood grow Go Forth Pest Control to $52 million

real_qa.q: What was Go Forth Pest Control's growth rate during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020?
real_qa.r: Go Forth Pest Control grew 68% in 2020 as an essential service, while losing approximately 20% of commercial business (which represented about 11% of total existing revenue). Residential business dominated after this shift, and the company was one step ahead because it had already built remote work capabilities and contactless service processes before the pandemic.
real_qa.requete: Go Forth Pest Control 2020 growth rate 68 percent

real_qa.q: What was Chase Hazelwood's most successful pest control acquisition and how much revenue did it grow to?
real_qa.r: His most successful acquisition was in Fayetteville, North Carolina, where he bought a $500,000 company that was making only $15,000 to $50,000 annually in net profit. The company had a completely underutilized customer base demanding the service type Hazelwood offered. He grew it from $500,000 to $3 million in four years by implementing his systems and processes.

real_qa.q: Why did Chase Hazelwood's acquisition of a Richmond, Virginia pest control company fail?
real_qa.r: The Richmond acquisition was disastrous because the previous owner was exceptionally influential and a tremendous salesman—he was the magic behind the business. When he left after the acquisition, the business imploded and Hazelwood lost almost all the acquisition money. The labor market was more expensive than North Carolina, and the city's traffic made the branch difficult to make profitable with the required staffing levels.
real_qa.requete: Chase Hazelwood Richmond Virginia acquisition disaster

real_qa.q: How much did Chase Hazelwood's Hickory, North Carolina pest control branch grow its revenue after acquisition?
real_qa.r: After acquiring a company in Hickory, Hazelwood's branch grew to $3 million in revenue with over 60% contribution margin and roughly 55-52% gross margin. The company paid for itself in three and a half years, and the building real estate itself was worth more than he paid for the entire acquisition after selling off excess acreage.
real_qa.requete: Chase Hazelwood Hickory North Carolina $3 million pest control

guest.bio_context: Chase Hazelwood is the third-generation owner of Go Forth Pest Control, which was founded by his grandfather Frank Goforth in 1959 after returning from World War II. He took over operations as general manager in 2008 at age 26, and later acquired majority control of the family business. Under his leadership, Go Forth Pest Control has grown to 300 employees with $52 million in annual revenue, operating from Maryland to Florida on the East Coast with additional branches in Texas and Tennessee. He also owns multiple other businesses including an HVAC plumbing company, HR consulting company, marketing company, and youth soccer club Carolina Core FC in High Point, North Carolina.
